newsitem.title: ITALY: BCI says no plans concerning Banco Napoli.
newsitem.headline: BCI says no plans concerning Banco Napoli.

text.p: Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) said it is not planning to take any action on Italy's biggest southern bank Banco di Napoli, due to be privatised by the end of the year.
Newspapers have speculated for weeks that BCI is interested in the privatisation of Banco di Napoli but the bank itself has previously declined to comment.
BCI managing director Luigi Fausti told reporters: "BCI has not planned and does not plan any intervention regarding Banco di Napoli.
"Our position on the problem has been clarified in the most precise terms a while ago," he added.
The Italian government won a confidence vote in the Senate (upper house) on Wednesday to convert into law a decree covering the rescue plan for the struggling Banco di Napoli.

The Treasury intends to offer 60 percent of the bank to the highest domestic or foreign bidder and potential buyers have until November 18 to declare an interest in the sale and until December 20 to make their final offer.
The southern bank, which last year unveiled record losses of 3.12 trillion lire ($2.1 billion), plunged a further 674 billion lire into the red in the first half of this year.
New management has been installed and it has launched a restructuring programme.
Another Italian bank thought to be interested, Banco Ambroveneto, repeated earlier on Wednesday that it had still not made any decision regarding Banco di Napoli.
"We have still not decided anything; it's not a small operation, it needs to be thought through," board member Gino Trombi told reporters at a meeting in Rome.
